title: Formal playing layout
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset: formal 16:10 widescreen in-game view for VIGINTI, a blackjack roguelike. Use the attached prior image only as reference for persimmon orange, muted turquoise, warm cream, hard three-tone cel shading, dark plum silhouettes, large tactile controls and a little game-show whimsy. This is a simplification pass and FUNCTIONAL UI LAYOUT, not environment illustration.
Simplify extremely: remove the large commercial title marquee, the studio camera, empty audience seats, stage trusses, floor patterns, confetti, APPLAUSE signs, starbursts across the playing surface, giant trophy decorations, dials, wheel, taped +1 gadget, and the second bottom action button. Background is just TWO broad matte theatrical flats with one quiet warm spotlight shadow. A very small smiling cardboard sun host is tucked near the top-right edge, subordinate to gameplay. The table is broad, clean, tilted slightly in perspective, filling nearly the whole frame. Card faces and all numerals are sharply readable, with no bloom and no glare on them. Sparse geometric 3D game objects, broad flat colours and contact shadows. Not a realistic casino, not ornate.
Fixed screen organisation:
Top 0-14% is a legible television SCORE FASCIA, facing the player frontally rather than steeply tilted. It has small "VIGINTI" at left, a prominent central "RUN WINNINGS" with "$1,240" in LARGE clear figures, and quieter "CASH $250", "ANTE $50", "INCREASE IN 4" at sides. RUN WINNINGS is the visual hierarchy leader.
Middle upper area reserved for dealer/draw OR scoring ledger depending on state.
The bottom half of table has EXACTLY THREE broad cream player card bays horizontally aligned, one left, one centre, one right. Beneath EACH bay, a large dedicated inset numeric counter for the current blackjack total, not a wager or currency counter. Left cards 10 spades plus 8 hearts, total "18". Centre cards 6 hearts plus 6 diamonds plus 9 clubs, total "21". Right cards 7 spades plus 6 clubs, total "13". These three counters remain present in every state. Bold standard corner rank/suit indices, normal Arabic digits. Fanned thin card stock with physical depth. No separate wagers below any hand.
Exactly SIX small relic plaques in side rails, three down left and three down right, no objects blocking cards. Compact simple tiny prize silhouettes in recessed sockets; clearly an inventory rather than six large elaborate sculptures.
Bottom 86-100% front lip: EXACTLY ONE prominent central button "STAND". Two clearly smaller utility buttons at bottom-left and bottom-right labelled "HAND SCORES" and "DECK". No extra bottom DRAW button. Drawing belongs to the central draw position on table, not bottom controls.
No poster captions, no annotations outside the game screen, no watermark. Keep main readable data prominent and decoration minimal. Preserve sharp cel-shaded three-dimensional perspective, not a flat wireframe.

State: PLAYING. Upper middle has a compact dealer pair centred at about x50% y24%, one visible 9 spades and one face-down blue/cream card. A small dealer blackjack counter "9" immediately beneath it; do NOT reveal the hidden card's contribution.
At about x50% y44% is a distinct draw tray with a single 4 diamonds card lifted just above its surface. Under it a small plain instruction "PLACE CARD". The draw tray has enough uncluttered horizontal clear space for several draw cards in later configurations. To either side are SMALL contextual action keys "HOLD" and "REDRAW", each with tiny charge marks; these are separate from the one bottom STAND action. Do not add more buttons.
All three player hand bays lie at y64-78% and their large 18 / 21 / 13 blackjack counters at y81%. Left and right bays get a restrained outline as legal placement targets; centre 21 stays calmly complete. Critical: the three totals must each sit directly under their respective cards. The prominent RUN WINNINGS is NOT one of these totals, and CASH is a separate balance.
The layout should feel calm, spacious, functional and deliberately designed for real play. The small host and set provide the game-show atmosphere at the periphery.

Ledger header "HAND 2 / 21". Three columns "CRITERION", "CASH", "MULT". Three rows:
"Viginti" "+$20" "+0.1"
"Pair" "+$12" "+0.1"
"Star Bead" "—" "+0.2"
Bottom ledger bar "ROUND CASH $42" and "MULT 1.5".
This is an in-progress shared round tally after scoring first and centre hands, NOT a separate per-hand payout. Do not add an equals payout or claim final result yet.
Centre player hand remains anchored above its own 21 counter, grows only around 15% and lifts slightly, with two matching 6 cards picked out in warm white and the 9 clubs subdued monochrome; keep all rank corners readable. Show the PAIR row as the current row via a simple amber underline; indicate the matching two sixes with a small local light. Left 18 and right13 hands remain visible, calmer and slightly desaturated; do not let the centre hand cover those totals. A slight darkened peripheral stage emphasizes arithmetic, without darkening the readable ledger or cards.
Bottom central STAND button is now visibly disabled, same physical location, no added action. HAND SCORES and DECK utility keys remain legible. The big run winnings header stays $1,240 until round payout is actually collected, Cash stays$250. No celebratory confetti, no giant payout numeral over cards, no extra mystery props.
Purpose is a credible numerical scoring state with enough space for a sequential ledger and persistent hand totals.
